claims.text: Achieving Hc above 100 Oe while retaining Tc above 300 K in fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti requires a magnetically distinct secondary phase rather than a single-phase fcc solid solution.
A Ti-rich ordered intermetallic or nanoscale Ti oxide can act as a domain-wall pinning center in an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
VEC criteria can be used to predict whether an HEA solid solution favors an fcc or bcc structure.
Optimizing Ti content using VEC will preserve the fcc matrix while allowing a secondary phase to form.
Aging between 600 K and 900 K will induce nanoscale Ti-rich precipitation or Ti-rich/Ti-poor chemical segregation in Fe-Co-Ni-Ti.
Homogenization at 1200 K followed by aging at 700 K for 24 hours will produce the proposed dual-phase microstructure.
The resulting secondary phase may consist of Ti-rich B2 or L12 precipitates or amorphous Ti-rich clusters embedded in an fcc matrix.
A nanoscale secondary phase can be embedded in a continuous matrix without necessarily eliminating the matrix phase.
A secondary phase with different saturation magnetization or anisotropy creates energy barriers to domain-wall motion.
Interfaces between the fcc matrix and Ti-rich precipitates introduce local strain and magnetic-anisotropy variations.
Ti locally reduces the magnetic moment relative to Fe and Co, producing magnetic contrast that pins domain walls.
Chemical interactions and compositional partitioning can alter the magnetic ground state or coupling in compositionally complex alloys.
The aged Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy will have Hc above 100 Oe because precipitates pin domain walls.
The aged alloy will retain a Curie temperature above 300 K.
Formation of a nonmagnetic or weakly magnetic Ti-rich phase will slightly lower saturation magnetization relative to the single-phase state.
The proposed treatment will produce precipitates 5–50 nm in size that are detectable by TEM and through XRD broadening or distinct peaks.
An unaged single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti baseline is expected to have Hc below 50 Oe because of orbital-moment suppression and the absence of pinning sites.
The design is expected to operate for Ti contents from 5 at.% to 20 at.%.
Above 25 at.% Ti, the alloy may transform to bcc or develop a continuous secondary-phase network that disrupts fcc continuity and magnetic percolation.
Precipitates larger than 100 nm may be ineffective pinning centers, while clusters smaller than 2 nm may not form magnetically distinct phases.

contradictions.description: An equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni-Ti initial state contains 25 at.% Ti, whereas the stated operating range is only 5–20 at.% Ti. Thus one explicitly proposed initial composition lies outside the hypothesis's own validity range.
